current_bottleneck: The 289e history-memory world-model backbone remains viable, and the 290 bracket already closed factorized per-cell output heads. 291a showed that a learned joint next-change support object is directionally better than cellwise bins, but a continuous support code is too entangled for the deterministic head to predict: shared structure collapsed, MR collapsed, and local-law realism stayed dead. The live bottleneck is now the support representation itself: it likely needs to be learned jointly but discretized.
last_result_summary: Iteration 125 ran 291a-v0, a joint-support world-model on top of the 289e backbone. It trained stably but scored only 1/11, with corr_ratio collapsing to 0.021 and MR ratio to 0.033. This falsified the naive continuous joint-support code and shifted the next step to a learned discrete joint support codebook on the same backbone.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 291b-v0: keep the 289e history-memory world-model backbone, but replace the continuous joint support code with a learned discrete codebook over next normalized-change panels.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, and 282b-v0 are the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11 in the two-level reset.
current_best_note: 282b is still the cleanest current Stage B objective frontier at 5/11, but 284b and 285a strengthen the conclusion that the real cap is now the Stage A support object rather than the Stage B weighting law.
